svg.aria-label: Fig 4. Planned voice agent. 1 a browser call, using WebRTC and Web Audio. 2 local speech-to-text, candidate Whisper or faster-whisper. 3 the agent turn: Muse picks the next line, and the agent says that it is an AI. 4 local text-to-speech, candidate Piper or Kokoro. Black tracks link 1 to 2 to 3 to 4. A dashed track takes the audio of the agent back into the call. A blue track is the call line to 5, our own mock payer rep, never a real payer. There is no phone line. A green track takes the result to 6, the call outcome card with the synthetic reference SYN-REF-0007, read back and logged. Planned, not built.

svg.text: Free tools only. No phone line. No real payer. Planned design, not built.
calls go only to our own mock
1 The call runs in the browser (WebRTC and Web Audio). There is no paid phone line.
2 Local speech-to-text turns the rep's voice into text. Candidates: Whisper or faster-whisper.
3 The agent picks the next turn with Muse. It says that it is an AI and announces the recording.
4 Local text-to-speech speaks the agent's turn. Candidates: Piper or Kokoro.
Each voice model gets a license check. Non-commercial voices are not allowed (D-018).
5 The rep is our own mock payer rep on the payer mock. Never call a real payer.
6 The agent records the rep name, the reference number and the time, and reads them back.
The call outcome updates the claim in the review console.
Tracks. Chevrons show the direction. black: audio and text between stations.
dashed: the agent's audio back into the call. blue: the call line to the mock rep.
green: the outcome of the call goes to the claim record.
